chunk_findings.detail:
In the `merge.forced` event the field named `unmet_gates` is populated with `gates.awaiting()`:
`{"sha": sha, "unmet_gates": gates.awaiting(), "approval": forced_by, "agent": agent}`.
The intent requires this event to name the unmet gates — the required gates that are blocking, which include gates with **failed** outcomes as well as gates lacking outcomes. The refusal path uses `list(gates.unmet)` for exactly this complete blocker set, and `awaiting()` is the value later used for `awaiting_gates`. So a forced merge over a required gate whose outcome is `failed` (the `unit_tests failed` case in the intent) can emit a `merge.forced` event whose `unmet_gates` field omits that failed gate, producing an audit trail that does not record the gate that justified the force.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/merge.py:merge_worktree

chunk_findings.detail: `assess` omits the required `merge` gate from `Assessment.states`. The code filters `_SELF` out of `unmet` (`if g != _SELF`) and then calls `gate_states(it, unmet)`. Before the merge the item has no record for `_SELF`, so `_SELF` is neither in `it.gates` nor in the `extra` iterable passed to `gate_states`. Because the filter exists precisely because `_SELF` appears in `v.unmet_gates` (the comment says it is the gate this very merge records, never unmet by the merge), the resulting `states` map fails its own documented contract: “every gate that has a record or is required.” Concrete input: an item with required gates `{"unit_tests", "merge"}` where `unit_tests` is failed and `merge` has no record. `v.unmet_gates` includes `merge`; `assess` produces `states` containing `{"unit_tests": "failed"}`, missing the required `merge` gate, so the merge record does not record the real state of every required gate.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/merge_force.py:assess

chunk_findings.detail: The fixture adds `"gates": ["dict"]` to the existing `merge.landed` event kind, but the change manifest does not update the corresponding `ddflow/templates/events` definition for `merge.landed` and has no `event_kind_field_added.merge.landed.gates` upgrade record. In the new warn/refuse path, a recorded `merge.landed` event will carry a `gates` field that the registered event kind does not declare, so event validation will reject it, or the schema/coherence test will report the template and fixture disagree. The fixture change needs a matching template and upgrade-record change.

chunk_findings.detail: This test does not actually prove single-use. The first call merges the same `T1`, then the second call reuses the same approval on that already-merged item; the test only asserts `again.exit == 3` and never checks that the refusal is because the approval was already spent. If a faulty implementation left approvals reusable, `merge_item` could still return exit 3 for the second call as “already merged,” so the single-use requirement could be broken while this test still passes.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_merge_force.py:test_the_approval_is_single_use

chunk_findings.detail: `authorise` returns a refusal whenever `force` is false, without checking `a.refuses`. For example, with `a = Assessment(mode="refuse", unmet={})` (all required gates settled) and `force=False`, it returns a message saying `[merge].require_gates = refuse and required gates are unsettled: . ...`, even though no gate is unsettled and the merge should be allowed without force. The same call with `mode="warn"` also produces a refusal that falsely claims require_gates is `refuse`. It should refuse only when `a.refuses` is true.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/merge_force.py:authorise

chunk_findings.detail: The hunk adds a new `"gates"` field to an already-existing event kind in the event_kinds fixture, but the change’s manifest contains no `event_field_added.*` upgrade record for that field (only `event_kind_added.merge.forced` and `knob_added.merge.require_gates` are present). A release-cut or template-derived fixture refresh will see the fixture field without a corresponding source/upgrade entry and will either omit the field or report an unreleased event schema change, violating the claimed r-upgrade-safe conformance [r-upgrade-safe].

chunk_findings.detail: The test only asserts that the second `_merge(repo, force=True, approval=ask)` call exits 3. After the first forced merge succeeds, the item T1 is already merged, so that second call would also exit 3 regardless of whether the approval was consumed. Concretely, a broken implementation that marks the approval used (so `test_a_forced_merge_with_an_approval_lands_and_records_merge_forced` still passes its `used == 1` assertion) but then fails to reject an already-used approval would not make this test fail. The test name claims to verify single-use enforcement, but the failure mode is not isolated from the already-merged failure.

chunk_findings.detail: The revised test still does not isolate “single-use”: it reuses the approval on a newly added item `T2`, whose merge command differs from the originally approved `T1` command. Because the approval is meant to be bound to the exact command and requesting agent, a defective implementation that marks the approval `used` but forgets to reject an already-used approval can still exit 3 on the `T2` call solely from the command-binding mismatch, leaving `used == 1` and no `T2` `worktree.merged` event. chunk_findings.detail: The new probe calls `_load(repo, "bot")` before the first forced merge and reuses that `log` object after `_merge` succeeds. `_merge` is a separate entry point and will not mutate the previously returned snapshot. Since `MF.authorise(log, ...)` decides whether the approval is spent from the argument it is given, a correct implementation will see the pre-merge `used == 0` state, return a stamp instead of `(None, "… is spent")`, and make the new assertion fail. Reload `log` after the successful merge before calling `MF.authorise`.

chunk_findings.detail: [r-upgrade-safe] `force` and `approval` are inserted before the existing `on_progress` parameter, changing the positional meaning of a pre-existing argument. A caller that previously invoked `merge(repo, cfg, item, wt, base, shell_cwd, agent, allow_empty, my_progress)` to pass a progress callback now binds `my_progress` to `force`, leaves `on_progress` as `None`, and gives `approval` its default. When required gates refuse, this call is then treated as a forced merge missing approval and is refused, even though the caller did not request a force; in warn mode the progress callback is silently dropped. Applause new options must be appended after `on_progress` or made keyword-only to preserve positional compatibility.
